response.response:
{
  "research_question": "How does mouse navigation performance vary across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) when assessed by Time-to-Target, Success rate, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "Sham stimulation produced the worst performance across all metrics: lowest Success rate (0.273), longest Time-to-Target (4.68 s), lowest Path Efficiency (0.308), slowest Average Speed (10.74 units/s), and lowest AD (0.236)",
    "Combined stimulation yielded the highest Success rate (0.780) and fastest Average Speed (12.83 units/s), with near-best Time-to-Target (2.56 s) and Path Efficiency (0.502)",
    "Bright Visual Only stimulation achieved the highest Path Efficiency (0.504) and second-highest Success rate (0.785), with competitive Time-to-Target (2.61 s)",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only showed intermediate performance, with Success rates of 0.685 and 0.673 respectively, and similar Time-to-Target values (~3.05-3.14 s)",
    "AD (angular dispersion) was highest in Combined (0.399) and Bright Visual Only (0.387) conditions, and lowest in Sham (0.236), suggesting more exploratory or variable movement patterns in active stimulation conditions",
    "Sample sizes varied substantially across paradigms: Combined dominated with n=48,846 (63.7% of data), while Sham had only n=3,505 (4.6% of data)"
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Success rate: Sham (0.273) vs. Combined (0.780) and Bright Visual Only (0.785) shows a 2.9-fold difference, representing the largest effect across any metric",
    "Time-to-Target: Sham (4.68 s) was 83% slower than Combined (2.56 s) and 79% slower than Bright Visual Only (2.61 s)",
    "Path Efficiency: Sham (0.308) was 64% lower than Combined (0.502) and Bright Visual Only (0.504), indicating substantially more indirect trajectories without stimulation",
    "AD: Sham (0.236) was 41% lower than Combined (0.399), suggesting markedly reduced angular variability in the absence of stimulation",
    "The gap between Sham and all active stimulation conditions is larger than differences among any active stimulation conditions, indicating that any stimulation substantially improves navigation performance"
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "Any form of stimulation—whether visual, ICMS, or combined—substantially improves mouse navigation performance compared to no stimulation. Combined stimulation and Bright Visual Only stimulation appear most effective, with Combined offering slight advantages in speed and Bright Visual Only in path directness. Notably, visual stimulation alone (especially bright) performs comparably to or better than ICMS alone, suggesting that sensory cues may be as or more important than intracortical microstimulation for this navigation task. The elevated angular dispersion in active stimulation conditions likely reflects more active exploration and course correction rather than impairment, as it coincides with better performance outcomes. The Sham condition's poor performance establishes a clear baseline for evaluating stimulation efficacy.",
  "limitations": [
    "Extreme imbalance in sample sizes across paradigms (Combined: 48,846 vs. Sham: 3,505) may affect precision of estimates for underrepresented groups",
    "No statistical tests (ANOVA, t-tests, or mixed models) were performed; all comparisons are descriptive and effect sizes are not formally quantified",
    "Mouse identity is not accounted for in these marginal summaries; individual differences and repeated measures structure are ignored",
    "Path Efficiency shows extreme range (max=29.8) suggesting possible outliers that may influence means",
    "Temperature and prompt template were fixed in this run, so generalizability to other LLM configurations is unknown",
    "Causal interpretation is limited without randomization verification or covariate adjustment",
    "AD interpretation as 'exploration' is inferential and not validated against behavioral coding"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a mixed-effects model with Mouse as a random intercept to account for within-mouse clustering, including Stim Paradigm as a fixed factor and adjusting for potential covariates. Perform pairwise comparisons with multiplicity correction (e.g., Tukey HSD) to identify which paradigm differences are statistically significant. Examine distributional properties of Path Efficiency and AD for outliers, and consider non-parametric alternatives if assumptions are violated. Finally, compute standardized effect sizes (Cohen's d) to quantify the practical magnitude of paradigm differences, particularly the Sham versus active stimulation contrasts."
}
